clean_source_blocks.text: Fifa seeks explanation over VAR official's hand gesture Fifa is seeking an explanation over a hand gesture made by video assistant referee Shaun Evans before Germany's 7-1 win over Curacao on Sunday. Before matches during the World Cup, Fifa has been briefly focusing on the officials as part of its world feed global coverage. First, the referee, and the rest of his team, have walked to the touchline and a graphic has been displayed with their names and roles. Then the picture has cut to a shot of the VAR team at the referee hub in Dallas. Rather than showing them at work and looking at their monitors, they have also briefly posed for the camera and their names have appeared on screen.
Fifa is seeking an explanation over a hand gesture made by video assistant referee Shaun Evans before Germany's 7-1 win over Curacao on Sunday.

FIFA is seeking an explanation over a hand gesture made by video assistant referee Shaun Evans before Germany's 7-1 win over Curaçao. When the camera cut to the VAR room on Sunday, Evans was standing in the screen-laiden zone with his arm by his side. The Australian arbiter then could be seen making the fingers of his right hand into an upside down 'OK' sign. According to the BBC, the gesture has two distinct meanings – one harmless and one deemed an expression of white supremacy. The incident was immediately subject to a huge amount of online speculation – FIFA is yet to issue an official response or explanation. However, BBC Sport has been told by sources that FIFA is looking for answers from the 38-year-old VAR official as to it's meaning.

Fifa are seeking answers after a World Cup VAR made a hand gesture used by white supremacists in a clip prior to the Germany v Curacao match on Sunday. Australian official Shaun Evans made the upside-down ‘OK’ symbol with his right hand as the broadcast feed cut to the ‘meet the team’ section for the VARs before kick-off. The gesture is used in the completely harmless ‘circle game’ but has also been used by far-right supporters and the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) added it to a list of hate symbols in 2019. Fifa are understood to be aware of the incident and seeking answers from Evans as to why he made the gesture.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Fifa seeks explanation over VAR official's hand gesture

Fifa is seeking an explanation over a hand gesture made by video assistant referee Shaun Evans before Germany's 7-1 win over Curacao on Sunday.

Before matches during the World Cup, Fifa has been briefly focusing on the officials as part of its world feed global coverage.

First, the referee, and the rest of his team, have walked to the touchline and a graphic has been displayed with their names and roles.

Then the picture has cut to a shot of the VAR team at the referee hub in Dallas.

Rather than showing them at work and looking at their monitors, they have also briefly posed for the camera and their names have appeared on screen.

When the camera cut to the VAR room on Sunday, Evans was standing with his arm by his side - and then could be seen making the fingers of his right hand into a upside down 'OK' sign.

Such a gesture has two very distinct meanings – one harmless and the other connected to an expression of white supremacy.

The incident was immediately subject to a huge amount of speculation on social media.

BBC Sport has approached Fifa multiple times for comment or some clarity but as yet there has been no official response.

However, BBC Sport has been told by sources that Fifa is looking for answers from the Australian VAR official.

Whatever the outcome, there was a noticeable change in approach for pre-match rituals after the Germany-Curacao game.

When the VAR hub was shown in three subsequent matches, the officials were already facing the monitors. No longer did we see them looking at the camera, although their names were still displayed.

The gesture made by Evans is very similar to the one used in the circle game, a prank which came to prominence in the US sitcom Malcolm in the Middle which became an internet meme.

An upside-down OK signal is made with the hand below the waist.

If another person looks at the hand they get a punch in the shoulder.

But in 2017 the OK sign also began to be used by the far right to communicate to each other.

The sign was added to a list of hate symbols by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) in 2019.

payload.title: Fifa pyytää selvitystä VAR-tuomarin käsimerkistä
payload.summary: Fifa selvittää australialaisen VAR-tuomarin Shaun Evansin tekemää käsimerkkiä ennen Saksan ja Curaçaon välistä MM-ottelua. Ele näkyi kansainvälisessä lähetyskuvassa ennen ottelun alkua.
payload.content:
Fifa pyytää selvitystä australialaiselta videotuomarilta Shaun Evansilta käsimerkistä, joka näkyi ennen Saksan 7–1-voittoa Curaçaosta sunnuntaina. Evans teki eleen, kun kansainvälinen lähetyskuva siirtyi ennen ottelun alkua VAR-huoneeseen Dallasissa sijaitsevassa tuomarikeskuksessa.

## Ele näkyi tuomarien esittelyssä

Ennen MM-otteluita Fifa on esitellyt ottelun erotuomariston lyhyesti kansainvälisessä lähetyskuvassaan. Ensin päätuomari ja muu kentällä toimiva tuomaristo ovat kävelleet sivurajalle, ja ruudulla on näytetty heidän nimensä ja roolinsa. Sen jälkeen lähetys on siirtynyt VAR-tiimiin Dallasissa sijaitsevassa tuomarikeskuksessa.

Tässä yhteydessä VAR-huoneen tuomarit eivät ole pelkästään näkyneet työpisteillään näyttöjen ääressä, vaan he ovat myös lyhyesti poseeranneet kameralle, samalla kun heidän nimensä on esitetty ruudulla. Evans nähtiin tilanteessa seisomassa VAR-alueella käsi sivullaan. Tämän jälkeen hän teki oikean kätensä sormilla ylösalaisin käännettyä OK-merkkiä muistuttavan eleen.

## Fifa hakee vastausta merkityksestä

Käsimerkki herätti nopeasti laajaa keskustelua verkossa. Lähteiden mukaan eleeseen liittyy kaksi erilaista tulkintaa. Sitä käytetään harmittomassa circle game -leikissä, mutta samaa symbolia ovat käyttäneet myös äärioikeistolaiset ja valkoista ylivaltaa kannattavat tahot. Anti-Defamation League lisäsi merkin vihasymbolien luetteloonsa vuonna 2019.

Fifa ei ole julkaissut asiasta virallista vastausta tai selitystä. Järjestön kerrotaan kuitenkin olevan tietoinen tapauksesta ja hakevan 38-vuotiaalta Evansilta vastausta siihen, miksi hän teki eleen lähetyskuvan aikana. Evans on australialainen erotuomari, joka toimi ottelussa videotuomarina.

## Tarkoitusta ei ole vahvistettu

Tapauksessa keskeistä on toistaiseksi se, että eleen tarkoitusta ei ole julkisesti vahvistettu. Fifa pyrkii selvittämään Evansin oman selityksen tilanteesta. Lähteissä ei esitetä, että ottelun lopputulos tai VAR-toiminnan tekniset ratkaisut olisivat selvityksen kohteena.

Ele näkyi kansainvälisessä lähetyksessä VAR-tuomarien esittelyn aikana.
